name: Sunreef
summary: A dive centre at The Wharf Mooloolaba running reef and wreck dives, humpback whale swims and whale watching, turtle snorkelling, sunset cruises and PADI courses. Boats leave via the Mooloolah River for the ex-HMAS Brisbane wreck, local reefs and Flinders Reef off Moreton Island. Whale watching, cruises and charters run on the vessel Whale One.
standouts: Longest established dive centre on the Sunshine Coast, with roots back to 1976
Whale encounters follow the Australian National Guidelines for Whale and Dolphin Watching (2017) and a Sunreef Code of Practice
Working with the University of the Sunshine Coast on a whale research project

trips.requirements: You must be able to swim. Not suitable if you are pregnant. Pre-existing medical conditions, prescription medication, injury or illness may rule out swimming, so contact Sunreef first. Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult at all times, on board or in the water, and must be strong swimmers. Children under 8 are not permitted on board. Each swimmer completes a Sunreef Swim with Whales Waiver. No wheelchair access, no drones and no alcohol on the vessel.

trips.title: Swim with Whales
trips.summary: A humpback whale swim from Mooloolaba. The crew look for whales from the boat, and swimmers enter the water only if the crew judge the whales' behaviour suitable and safe, otherwise the whales are watched from the boat. Masks, snorkels, fins and wetsuits are provided, and guests should allow at least 4 hours from start to finish.

checkNotes: About 41 pages were read, so some products were not opened: Self Reliant Diver, Divemaster, Instructor Development Course, First Aid, O2 and CPR training, Private Training, PADI Women's Dive Day, International Dive Trips (the site says they run annually), Christmas Lights and Christmas Boat Parade cruises, New Years Eve cruises, Gear Servicing, and the Hire pages (jet skis, boats, kayaks, stand up paddle boards; equipment rental rather than guided trips, so not recorded). The Cultural Cruises page names three cruises (Tallo Billa, Deep Listening at Dawn, Mudjimba Dreamtime) but gives no times, prices, duration or booking details, so they are not recorded. Left out as dated: the Ex-HMAS Brisbane 20th Anniversary Dive (a one-off event marking 20 years since the 2005 scuttling; $121 including anniversary merchandise, about 5 hours, check in 2:30pm); it is likely past, so it was not recorded as a current trip. Bookings: every trip is sold through a booking calendar embedded on its own page (a Rezdy widget on sunreef.rezdy.com), plus Book Now buttons. Those Rezdy pages were not opened, so prices and times that appear only there are missing. The Rezdy alias is sunreef; the same account sells the Whale One trips. For trips with no per-trip link, bookingLinks holds the page the widget sits on. Whale One: the site says 'Whale One operates out of Sunreef' and also speaks of 'our vessel Whale One'; Whale One has its own Facebook and Instagram pages. Confirm it is Sunreef's own vessel and that the whale watching, sunset cruise and charters are Sunreef's trips. Swimming with whales: no permit or licence is stated on the page; it cites the Australian National Guidelines for Whale and Dolphin Watching (2017) and a Sunreef Code of Practice. Confirm the Queensland permit before publishing. Ex-HMAS Brisbane: diving on the wreck is external only since Tropical Cyclone Alfred (9 March 2025) and commercial works on the site; trips and courses that use the wreck should be checked before publishing. Claims not repeated: 'Australia's first swim with humpback whales operator', encounter-rate and sighting guarantee wording on the whale pages, and 'one of the biggest employers of full-time dive professionals in Australia'. The home page shows an Eco Certified (Ecotourism) logo with no level or certifier named in text, so it is not listed as a standout. Contact: phone and email are from the home page; a second address, dive@sunreef.com.au, is in a mailto link on the pages. Shop hours on the home page are 8am to 5pm Monday to Saturday and 8am to 4pm Sunday. The page footers still read 2020. Photos: credit lines appear on the ex-HMAS Brisbane page (Colin Baker; Matt Shepherd's nudibranch site) and the Nudibranch Double Dive page (Gary Cobb), so those photos were left out. Other pages carry no credit lines, but the numbered underwater photos may come from the same photographers, so a person should confirm ownership.
